justification: P2b wires the Housing-SEPP/LMR eligibility engine into the LIVE capacity ceiling, raising the upper 'subject to a DA' figure where the lot is genuinely eligible (townhouses on R2 statewide; apartments in a TOD catchment). This changes user-facing yield upward, so critical tier. Includes a 1-line engine correctness fix so R1/R2 mid-rise flats are catchment-gated like R3/R4 (they were not), preventing an apartment over-claim on every R2 lot.

pre_impl.existing_data: The merged eligibility engine (evaluate_eligibility) returns per-form eligibility from authoritative gates (776 LMR area, 452 dual-occ, 752/759 TOD). The brief ceiling was the base zone-tier ∩ LEP-permitted form. lot width comes from planning_controls.lot_dimensions.frontage_m; heritage from _is_heritage_land(controls, heritage_postgis).
pre_impl.assumption_mismatch: The ported frontend logic gated only residential_flat_r3r4 on the TOD catchment, treating R1/R2 residential flats as available anywhere in the (near-everywhere) 776 LMR area — which would surface an apartment ceiling on every R2 lot. Fixed: all residential_flat forms are mid-rise and require the catchment.
pre_impl.new_vs_existing: No new file, no new query. _lmr_uplift_form delegates to the engine and maps the densest eligible form to an engine ceiling form; _realistic_forms takes the denser of the base ceiling and that uplift. Both brief assembly paths now pass lat/lng/lot-area/lot-width/heritage. The engine TOD gate changes residential_flat_r3r4 -> residential_flat (1 line).
pre_impl.external_source_error: The uplift relies on the engine's live ePlanning layer queries (776/452/752/759) and a standards DB read. _lmr_uplift_form wraps the whole engine call in try/except and returns None on any error, and the engine itself fails each gate to its conservative value, so a gov-API or DB failure yields no uplift and the base zone-tier ceiling stands (never an over-claim).
pre_impl.frontend_type: Backend only. The capacity ceiling fields (max_permitted_form / max_permitted_dwellings) keep their types; only their value rises when the lot is genuinely eligible. The capacity card already renders the ceiling as the subject-to-DA upper bound, so no frontend interface change is needed.
pre_impl.user_failure_mode: Before: a TOD lot under-stated its apartment potential and an R2 lot under-stated its townhouse potential. After: the ceiling rises to the genuine LMR upside, framed subject-to-a-DA. If a gate fails, the user simply sees the base zone-tier ceiling (a conservative under-state), never a denser form than the lot is eligible for.

functions.name: _lmr_uplift_form
functions.input: the zone code, lat, lng, lot area, lot width and a heritage flag for the subject lot
functions.output: the densest engine ceiling form the eligibility engine found eligible, or None when there is no uplift
functions.if_none: any engine error, or no eligible uplift form, returns None so the base zone-tier ceiling stands unchanged

functions.name: _realistic_forms
functions.input: the zone code, LGA name, optional excluded_forms set and the optional uplift_form from the engine
functions.output: a tuple of (as_of_right_form, ceiling_form) where the ceiling is the denser of the base form and the uplift
functions.if_none: with no permitted form and no uplift it returns the conservative ('dwelling_house','dwelling_house') pair

functions.name: evaluate_eligibility
functions.input: zone, lot area and width, lat, lng, a heritage flag and optional pre-fetched gate inputs
functions.output: per-development-type eligibility with all residential-flat forms now gated on the TOD catchment
functions.if_none: a non-residential zone or an unavailable standards table returns an empty list, fail-safe to base controls

values: N/A - no regulatory values are hardcoded. The uplift form comes from the engine's live eligibility (thresholds read from housing_sepp_standards); the form-name mapping is engine-internal identifiers, not planning values.
queries: N/A - this change adds no new database query; it delegates to the already-reviewed eligibility-engine query and reads live ePlanning layers via the existing fetchers.

break_it.scenario: An R2 lot that is in the (near-everywhere) 776 LMR area but NOT in a TOD catchment
break_it.what_happens: Gating R1/R2 flats on LMR-area only would show an apartment ceiling on essentially every R2 lot
break_it.repro: pytest tests/test_housing_sepp_eligibility.py::test_all_residential_flats_require_tod_catchment ; live Five Dock R2 -> ceiling multi_dwelling_housing (townhouses), not residential flat
break_it.how: the engine now gates every residential_flat form on in_tod, so an R2 lot outside a catchment tops out at the low-rise LMR form (townhouses)

break_it.scenario: A heritage conservation-area lot that is otherwise LMR/TOD eligible
break_it.what_happens: The ceiling could rise to townhouses or apartments on heritage land where the LMR reforms do not apply
break_it.repro: pytest tests/test_housing_sepp_eligibility.py::test_heritage_suppresses_lmr_forms_but_not_base_forms ; live Haberfield heritage -> ceiling dual_occupancy
break_it.how: the heritage flag (from _is_heritage_land) suppresses requires_lmr_area forms, so the uplift returns None and the base ceiling stands

break_it.scenario: The eligibility engine errors or times out while assembling the brief (ArcGIS or DB failure)
break_it.what_happens: A naive uplift could crash the brief or invent a ceiling that is not actually eligible
break_it.repro: _lmr_uplift_form wraps evaluate_eligibility in try/except (see services/intelligence_brief.py:1097); on error it returns None
break_it.how: on any error _lmr_uplift_form returns None and _realistic_forms keeps the base zone-tier ceiling — fail-safe, never over-claims

break_it.scenario: The uplift form is actually LESS dense than the base zone-tier ceiling for the lot
break_it.what_happens: Naively replacing the base with the uplift could LOWER a legitimate ceiling
break_it.repro: code review of _realistic_forms — it only swaps when the uplift's density index is lower (denser) than the base
break_it.how: _realistic_forms takes the denser of the two by _ENGINE_FORM_DENSITY index, so the ceiling can only rise, never fall, from the uplift

break_it.scenario: A small or narrow lot inside a TOD/LMR area that cannot meet any LMR form's lot standard
break_it.what_happens: An uplift could appear on a lot too small to support any denser form
break_it.repro: live small lot R2 (380 m²/9 m) -> uplift None, ceiling dual_occupancy
break_it.how: the engine's lot-size/width and data-gap gates mark every uplift form ineligible, so _lmr_uplift_form returns None

post_merge.manual_verify: Run live briefs across contexts (verified: Ashfield/R4 in-TOD -> residential flat; Five Dock R2 -> multi-dwelling townhouses; Haberfield heritage -> dual occ; small lot -> dual occ). P3 migrates the LEP/SEPP tab onto the same engine and retires the mock station lists + dead servers. The manor_house and (now-fixed) R1/R2-flat data assumptions should be reconciled in housing_sepp_standards separately.
